forces.title: Significant global infrastructure investment deficit drives private capital demand.
forces.description: A cumulative $106 trillion in infrastructure investments is needed globally through 2040, far exceeding public sector capacity. This immense demand for both traditional and next-generation assets creates a substantial opportunity for private capital. This positions infrastructure investment vehicles as a critical solution to bridge this funding gap, enhancing their relevance and growth prospects.
forces.source_title: Infrastructure: Investing to support global growth

forces.title: Limited partners increase infrastructure allocations for diversification and returns.
forces.description: A strong majority of limited partners (LPs) (51%) plan to increase their infrastructure allocations over the next three years, driven by the desire for portfolio diversification (68%) and improved returns (52%). This sustained institutional investor interest fuels robust fundraising for infrastructure investment vehicles, underscoring their appeal as a stable yet growing asset class.
forces.source_title: Infrastructure: Investing to support global growth

forces.title: Infrastructure investment shifts towards higher-risk, higher-return strategies.
forces.description: The infrastructure investment industry is maturing, marked by a growing willingness of general partners and LPs to move up the risk curve from traditional core to core-plus and value-added strategies. This shift, driven by the pursuit of higher returns, signifies a structural evolution in asset allocation and a broadening of investment opportunities for infrastructure funds beyond stable, regulated assets.
forces.source_title: Infrastructure: Investing to support global growth

forces.title: Megafunds enable large capital deployment in European infrastructure.
forces.description: The robust growth in European infrastructure fundraising, which rose by approximately 65% in 2025, was significantly enabled by "megafunds" ($5 billion or more in committed capital). These large funds facilitate substantial capital deployment, allowing for bigger and more complex transactions, which is crucial for addressing the continent's evolving infrastructure needs and investor appetite for scale.
forces.source_title: Infrastructure: Investing to support global growth

forces.title: Rising interest rates temporarily slowed infrastructure fundraising in 2023.
forces.description: In 2023, infrastructure fundraising experienced a temporary fall after a record high in 2022, primarily due to rising interest rates that prompted some investors to temporarily pivot towards debt-based alternatives. This demonstrates a cyclical sensitivity to macroeconomic conditions, though the market corrected back to an upward course in 2024 and 2025, suggesting resilience in the long-term outlook for investment vehicles.
forces.source_title: Infrastructure: Investing to support global growth

forces.title: AI-driven optimization enhances underlying infrastructure asset economics.
forces.description: AI-enabled asset optimization platforms are improving the financial viability of physical infrastructure assets such as grids and battery storage systems. By increasing revenue from existing hardware, unlocking additional capacity without new construction, and reducing operational costs, AI directly enhances the economics of these assets, making them more attractive targets for infrastructure capital and associated investment vehicles.
forces.source_title: The Private Capital Opportunity in AI-Enabled Climate and Sustainability Sectors

forces.title: Diversified investment into physical and digital AI-embedded assets.
forces.description: Infrastructure capital is increasingly being deployed into physical assets with embedded AI, such as smart grids, energy storage systems, and data centers, rather than being confined to traditional infrastructure types. This represents a structural shift, expanding the definition of investable infrastructure and requiring investors to consider technological integration as a core component of asset value, impacting the scope of infrastructure investment vehicles.
forces.source_title: The Private Capital Opportunity in AI-Enabled Climate and Sustainability Sectors

viewpoints.title: Private capital increasingly critical for meeting global infrastructure investment needs.
viewpoints.description: Private capital is increasingly crucial to meet global infrastructure investment requirements, projected at $106 trillion through 2040 for both traditional and next-generation assets. Public sector funding alone is insufficient, leading to record fundraising for infrastructure in 2025, reaching nearly $200 billion. This indicates a strong positive shift towards private sector involvement in financing essential infrastructure, highlighting the growing importance of investment vehicles.
viewpoints.source_title: Infrastructure: Investing to support global growth

viewpoints.title: Limited partners increase infrastructure allocations for diversification and returns.
viewpoints.description: Limited partners (LPs) are significantly increasing their allocations to infrastructure investments, with 51% planning to raise allocations over the next three years, making it the leading asset class for increased commitment. Key drivers include diversification (68% of LPs) and expected return improvements (52% of LPs), highlighting infrastructure investment vehicles' growing strategic importance in institutional portfolios.
viewpoints.source_title: Infrastructure: Investing to support global growth

viewpoints.title: Investors shift towards higher-risk infrastructure strategies for enhanced returns.
viewpoints.description: As the infrastructure sector matures, investors are increasingly willing to move up the risk curve from "traditional core" to "core plus" and "value added" strategies. This shift is driven by a pursuit of higher returns, with value-added and core-plus fundraising growing significantly (30% and 390% respectively), while core infrastructure declined by nearly 19%. This indicates a growing appetite for more complex, higher-upside infrastructure deals and vehicles.
viewpoints.source_title: Infrastructure: Investing to support global growth

viewpoints.title: AI-driven asset optimization enhances infrastructure capital investment appeal.
viewpoints.description: AI-enabled asset optimization is making underlying infrastructure economics more attractive, drawing increased private capital into sectors like battery energy storage systems (BESS) and independent power production. Examples such as KKR’s acquisition of Zenobē and Brookfield’s acquisition of Neoen demonstrate that AI-driven improvements in asset performance are a key thesis for infrastructure investors, fostering confidence in the sector and the vehicles that finance it.
viewpoints.source_title: The Private Capital Opportunity in AI-Enabled Climate and Sustainability Sectors
